title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 341 (Liability under sections 339 and 340 to extend to partners or directors in firms or companies)

content.overview: Where a declaration under section 339 or an order under section 340 is made in respect of a firm or body corporate, the Tribunal shall also have power to make a declaration under section 339, or pass an order under section 340, as the case may be, in respect of any person who was at the relevant time a partner in that firm or a director of that body corporate.
content.glance: Tribunal may extend s. 339 fraudulent-trading declarations and s. 340 misfeasance orders to partners of firms and directors of bodies corporate.
content.study: Section 341 pierces the firm or company veil for liability under sections 339 and 340. If the Tribunal has made a fraudulent-trading declaration (s. 339) or a misfeasance/breach-of-trust order (s. 340) against a firm or body corporate, it may also make the corresponding declaration or order against any person who was a partner in that firm or a director of that body corporate at the relevant time. The provision ensures that natural persons behind the firm or company cannot escape personal responsibility solely by the interposition of the entity.

sections.heading: Extension of liability
sections.body: Partners of firms and directors of bodies corporate may be made subject to s. 339 declarations or s. 340 orders where the entity itself is so ordered.

provisions.title: Liability under sections 339 and 340 to extend to partners or directors in firms or companies

examples.title: Partner of delinquent firm
examples.body: A firm that managed the company’s affairs is ordered under s. 340 to restore misapplied funds. Under s. 341 the Tribunal may also order a partner of that firm who was in office at the relevant time to restore.

hypotheticals.question: Can a director of a body corporate that was ordered under s. 339 be personally declared liable?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. Section 341 expressly empowers the Tribunal to make a corresponding declaration against a director of the body corporate at the relevant time.
